Q: multiple indipendent variable for linear regression in Google Sheets A:

Your problem is not the syntax — the regression is not identifiable.

In your data, field1 is constant (all values are 33).

With calculate_b = TRUE, LINEST automatically adds an intercept column (all 1s).

So you end up with two perfectly collinear columns:

  • • intercept = (1,1,1,…)

  • • field1 = (33,33,33,…) = 33 × intercept

This makes the design matrix singular, so the coefficients are not uniquely defined.

That’s why LINEST either returns #N/A or numerically unstable values.

To fix it:

Option A — keep the intercept, drop the constant predictor

=LINEST(C2:C8, B2:B8, TRUE)

Option B — keep the constant predictor, but disable the intercept

=LINEST(C2:C8, A2:B8, FALSE)

In practice, regression tools that explicitly check for “singular matrix / constant predictors” will stop and report this condition instead of returning misleading coefficients (for example STATS_LINEAR in Google Sheets reports it as “singular matrix or constant predictors”).

Q: SQL Query to Filter Rows Above Average While Removing Consecutive Qualifying Rows A:

I'm not super versed in animal based databases, but if it supports window functions, a potential solution can be something like:

WITH data AS (
        SELECT  1 AS id, 1 AS A
        UNION ALL
        SELECT  2, 7
        UNION ALL
        SELECT  3, 3
        UNION ALL
        SELECT  4, 4
        UNION ALL
        SELECT  5, 5
        UNION ALL
        SELECT  7, 4
        UNION ALL
        SELECT  10, 4
)
SELECT  *
FROM    (
        SELECT  *
        ,   LAG(A) OVER(ORDER BY ID) AS prevA
        ,   AVG(A * 1.0) OVER() avgConst
        FROM    data d
    ) x
WHERE   A >= avgConst
AND (prevA < avgConst OR prevA IS NULL)

I've added some more data to create better samples.

To get the previous value, you can use LAG(A), then it's easy to have a WHERE which checks so current value is above the average and previous one isn't. Just make sure that A cannot be NULL. You can also use something like: COALESCE(prevA, 0) < avgConst where 0 is the value which A cannot be lower than.

Output:

id A prevA avgConst
2 7 1 4
4 4 3 4

Q: What does "prong" mean in the context of Zig language? A:

The second meaning of prong in its Wiktionary entry is

(sometimes figurative) A branch; a fork.

- the two prongs of a river
- the second prong of the argument

It clearly refers to a branch of a switch statement

Q: React native - how to fix Java.lang Double cannot be cast to java.lang.Boolean A:

In my case, I had installed expo-router dependencies directly from the npm registry instead of using the expo cli to download versions that work with expo

Incorrect

yarn install expo-router react-native-safe-area-context react-native-screens expo-linking expo-constants expo-status-bar

Correct

yarn expo install expo-router react-native-safe-area-context react-native-screens expo-linking expo-constants expo-status-bar

https://docs.expo.dev/router/installation/#quick-start

Q: Rocky Linux 9: mod_wsgi logging to stderr fails with complete silence A:

Quick test with the latest Rocky 10.1 with stock python3-mod_wsgi-5.0.0-4.el10.x86_64 shows that it has been fixed. RPM SPEC doesn't have much of configure options / patches so I assume it's the mod_wsgi 4.7.1 -> 5.0.0. Now the output has the logger line.

[wsgi:error] [pid 6301:tid 6304] RAW STDERR TEST 
[wsgi:error] [pid 6301:tid 6304] FISH
[wsgi:error] [pid 6301:tid 6304] [remote xxx.yyy.xxx.yyy:12334] logger.ERROR

Also noticed that using the global WSGIRestrictStdout, WSGIRestrictStderr and WSGIPythonUnbuffered crashed the httpd. R9 is probably broken more than I know.

This is not a question per se, but I hope someone would have shared this before me and would have saved a lot of fustration.

Additional observations along the way:

  • don't use logging.basicConfig() with mod_wsgi

  • mod_wsgi might init the root logging instance which does affect the child ones
